comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA study-programme page publishes a complete 180-EC curriculum: twelve named first-year components totalling 60 EC; twelve named second-year components totalling 60 EC; and a third year with 30 EC of electives, 6 EC of philosophy and ethics, 6 EC of Robots that Learn and an 18-EC graduation project. The official overview confirms the programme’s integration of computing, cognitive science, mathematical foundations, language and speech technology, machine learning and intelligent behaviour. The 30-EC elective space is preserved as a bounded curriculum component without inventing course titles.

questions: How can intelligent systems learn, reason, plan and act?
What can computational models reveal about human thought, perception, language and the brain?
How should AI systems be designed and evaluated for people and society?

alternatives.label: Artificial Intelligence, Cognition & Intelligent Systems
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Artificial Intelligence programme combining programming, mathematical reasoning, data, machine learning, neural networks, robotics, decision-making and algorithms with cognition, language, ethics, experimental methods and human-centred communication.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum integrates computational AI with substantial cognitive-science and intelligent-systems study, so the label names all three organising elements.
progression: Programming, mathematics, data, brain-and-behaviour and research foundations precede advanced algorithms, optimisation, deep learning, robotics, cognition and psycholinguistics. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Computational AI & autonomous systems
alternatives.concept: A computational AI route centred on programming, algorithms, software, mathematical and statistical modelling, machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, optimisation, robotics, computer vision, databases, networks and autonomous agents.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum's dense programming, algorithms, mathematics, learning, optimisation and robotics sequence supports a computational and autonomous-systems label.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match and the cognitive route, this curriculum replaces much of the psychology, neuroscience and philosophy content with databases, networks, software development, advanced algorithms, reinforcement learning and numerical methods.
progression: Research, mathematics, data and database foundations precede programming-intensive software, robotics, algorithms, optimisation, reinforcement learning and deep learning. Programming and Mathematical Methods precede every course that formally requires them, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Cognitive AI, language & neuroscience
alternatives.concept: A cognitive AI route centred on computational models of mind, brain and behaviour, combining cognition, neuroscience, perception, language, psychology and philosophy with programming, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, logic, mathematics and experimental research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme combines AI methods with a sustained sequence in cognitive science, neuroscience, psychology, language and philosophy.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad and computational alternatives, this route gives substantially greater weight to neurobiology, lifespan and social psychology, perception, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, philosophy of mind, agency and advanced behavioural research.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour, neurobiology, mathematics, programming and statistical foundations precede perception, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, deep learning, computer vision, algorithms and advanced research. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

candidates.label: Computational AI and autonomous intelligent systems

selection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two generator-backed and feasible organising directions: computational AI and autonomous intelligent systems; and cognitive AI, language and neuroscience. Each produces material curricular consequences and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

blocks: Both provide a foundational introduction to programming for later computational study.
Both develop systematic software design and implementation practices.
Advanced Algorithms develops systematic computational problem solving; it is more algorithmically specialised than the UvA course.
Both directly cover data structures, algorithms and computational complexity.
Both use mathematical optimisation methods for computational and AI problems.
Both provide a dedicated introduction to machine-learning methods and model evaluation.
Both provide substantial neural-network theory and implementation, with UCR also extending into deep learning.
Both provide dedicated robotics study; UCR focuses on kinematics, manipulation and motion planning, while UvA emphasises learning robots.
Both directly cover image processing and computer-vision methods.
Both develop linear-algebra foundations through matrices, vectors and transformations.
Both develop formal logic and discrete reasoning for computing and AI.
Both combine probability and statistical inference for data-driven modelling.
Both develop mathematical methods for algorithms; UCR emphasises computational and numerical techniques.
Both investigate language processing; UCR focuses on human psycholinguistics rather than computational NLP.
Both provide philosophical analysis of mind and intelligence; UCR does not reproduce the full dedicated ethics component.
Both critically examine safety, fairness, responsibility, regulation and societal consequences of AI.
Both provide explicit first-year academic and professional formation; UCR PPD is broader than the AI-specific practicum.

notes.text: The UvA Artificial Intelligence bachelor provides a tightly integrated 180-EC sequence across programming, mathematics, statistics, machine learning, neural networks, cognitive modelling, natural-language processing, computer vision, logic, robotics, ethics, projects and an 18-EC graduation project. UCR can assemble strong interdisciplinary AI pathways with substantial programming, algorithms, data, machine learning, robotics, cognition, ethics and research, but it does not reproduce the same continuous specialist sequence or dedicated components in MLOps, probabilistic graphical models and computational NLP.
